questions.q: What attitude does Frankl say helped some prisoners survive the camps?
a: A kind of indifference to death and the future
An unshakable belief that they would be rescued soon
A determination to escape at any cost
A hope that conditions would improve within weeks
questions.why: Lesson 1 says prisoners had to be okay with dying at any moment, shielding their minds from terror.

questions.q: What does logotherapy say about the meaning of your life?
a: It is unique to you and shifts with your decisions and situation
It is fixed at birth and simply has to be discovered
It is the same universal meaning for every person
It can only be found after your basic needs are met
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares meaning to the best chess move, which depends on the particular situation on the board.

questions.q: According to the summary, what determines how much meaning you experience?
a: The responsibility you take for the decisions you make
The amount of suffering you have endured in life
The degree of comfort and security you achieve
The number of people who admire your accomplishments
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the responsibility you bring to your decisions shapes how large your sense of meaning is.

Avoiding every situation that could trigger your fear
Repeating positive affirmations until the fear disappears
Analyzing childhood memories to explain the fear
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes flipping fear around by attempting to force the feared outcome to happen.

questions.q: How did Frankl find a moment of meaning during a forced nighttime march?
a: He thought of his wife and imagined her face in the clouds
He focused on the food he would eat after the war
He recited passages from books he had memorized
He imagined escaping and returning to his hometown
questions.why: Lesson 2 recounts that thinking of his wife let him find bliss even while walking barefoot over icy rocks.
